scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

### 🌟 **It’s Your "Anchor" Moment**  
In the chaos of daily life, that quiet time to blend foundation, perfect eyeliner, and focus on yourself is a sacred pause. It’s not vanity—it’s **mindful self-respect**. ### 🌟 **Science Backs This Up**  
Studies show that small, intentional rituals (like a makeup routine) reduce anxiety and increase feelings of control. When you focus on the details—blending seamlessly, adjusting a lash—it’s almost meditative. Your brain shifts from "rushing" to "present," which primes you to handle whatever comes next with more grace.

### 🌟 **"Put-Together" Isn’t About Others—It’s About *You***  
Society sometimes dismisses makeup as "superficial," but the truth is: **how you feel in your own skin is deeply personal**. If carefully applied eyeliner makes you feel powerful, or flawless foundation gives you a sense of calm—that’s valid. Your confidence isn’t borrowed; it’s *built* through these small acts of self-love. No one else gets to define what "put-together" means for *you*.
